name: Duchy of the Archipelago
native: Δουκάτο του Αιγαίου Πελάγους (Doukáto tou Aigaíou Pelágous)
alt: Duchy of Naxos and the Cyclades

predecessors.name: Byzantine Empire
predecessors.text: Naxos, 'largely captured' by Marco Sanudo in 1207 and occupied entire in 1210, then Melos 'and the rest of the Cyclades'

successors.name: Ottoman Empire
successors.text: the Cyclades of the duchy, expropriated by Murad III in 1579 (infobox)

rulers.name: Joseph Nasi
rulers.title: duke by appointment of the Ottoman Sultan

ledger.x: 1207: Marco Sanudo founds the Duchy of the Archipelago on Naxos.
1210: with Naxos entirely occupied Sanudo conquers Melos and the rest of the Cyclades.
1278: Licario's Byzantines take most of the duchy's islands (bridging year, moved from 1277 after review).
1310: the Byzantines give up their Cycladic gains.
1383: the Crispo overthrow the Sanudo heirs.
1566: Selim II deposes the last Crispo duke.

wars.name: Licario's Aegean campaign
wars.outcome: Licario's fleet takes Karystos (1276), Skopelos (1277), Skyros, Skiathos, Amorgos and later Kythera, Kea, Santorini, Sifnos and Serifos; the conquests 'proved temporary only'; the duchy page has the Byzantines relinquish their gains in 1310.

wars.name: Catalan raid on the Duchy of the Archipelago
wars.outcome: 'In 1317 the Catalan Company raided the remnants of the duchy'; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Ottoman conquest of the Duchy of the Archipelago
wars.outcome: Ottoman suzerainty from 1537, Giacomo IV deposed in 1566 and Joseph Nasi installed, annexation by Murad III in 1579.

certainty.note: Island polities: the pages name islands, never sea limits; the Cyclades are drawn as whole islands on a grid of 15 km cells, so the smaller islands are approximate throughout.
